teams.heading: Italy captain Nicotera brands Fiji more beatable, yet a side to fear
teams.body: Italy captain Giacomo Nicotera told his pre-match press conference that the world ranking is an honest guide and called Fiji the more winnable assignment. He also warned that Jake White's side carry incredible individuals, many playing in France's Top 14. He said Italy will need control and organisation in Saturday's Round 6 Test in Udine. Both sides arrive without a win. The Italian federation notes that defeat, or victory without a bonus, would send Fiji into a Twickenham rematch with Italy in the sixth-place final.

lead.why: The Latui rout and Fiji's selection have both run, so the freshest item on Saturday's Test is Italy's captain sizing up Fiji.

teams.heading: Will Stuart back from ruptured Achilles as England chase All Black scalp
teams.body: The BBC's Mike Henson ties England's revival to Will Stuart, the England and British and Irish Lions star who missed the start of the year with a ruptured Achilles tendon. Without him England endured a terrible Six Nations and five straight defeats. Since his return they have scored 20 tries against Australia and Japan and sit top of the Nations Championship for points scored and entries into the opposition 22. Saturday's visitors arrive sore after a first defeat by Wales in 73 years.

lead.why: A fresh England storyline tying Stuart's return from injury to the side's attacking revival before the All Blacks test.

teams.heading: Marc Duzan warns France against underestimating struggling Pumas after Springbok win
teams.body: Midi Olympique senior reporter Marc Duzan concedes the Pumas arrive in poor shape: eighth in the world rankings, they were beaten 42-12 by Ireland a fortnight ago, lost 14-19 in Italy last weekend and are without the injured Juan Cruz Mallía, whom he rates their best player. Writing in Rugbyrama after France's 21-19 defeat of the Springboks at Saint-Denis, he nonetheless calls taking them lightly an enormous mistake. Victory would earn the Bleus a Nations Championship final at Twickenham the following weekend.

lead.why: The day's fresh France-centred preview: a named Midi Olympique writer warns the Bleus off complacency against a struggling Argentina, with a Twickenham final at stake.

teams.heading: Sam Illo ruled out as Thomas Clarkson joins Ireland bench against Springboks
teams.body: Connacht tighthead prop Sam Illo failed to complete return-to-play protocols after the concussion he took in last week's win over Fiji, SA Rugby Magazine reports. That forces Ireland head coach Andy Farrell into a late change for Saturday's Test. Leinster's Thomas Clarkson takes the No. 18 jersey on the bench and is in line for his first appearance of the Nations Championship's second leg. Connacht's Finlay Bealham has joined the squad as emergency cover. South Africa have promoted lock Franco Mostert to start in place of the injured Ruan Nortjé.

lead.why: The Fiji Latui result has already run, so this concussion-forced change to the senior matchday 23 is the freshest hard news about the Springbok Test.

teams.heading: Nicotera admits Italy's low spell, eyes Fiji test to rebuild confidence
teams.body: Italy captain Giacomo Nicotera admitted at his pre-match press conference that the squad still carry a nagging frustration from defeats by South Africa and Argentina, two games he called emotionally hard for different reasons. Calling it a low spell, he said Italy need one match to rediscover positive feelings and confidence. On Saturday's opponents in Udine, the Trieste native called Fiji a more approachable match, true to the world rankings, but warned of incredible individuals playing in France's Top 14.

lead.why: The captain's pre-match press conference is the only new Italy item, as the lineup and Miotti stories have already run.

teams.heading: Stafford McDowall to captain Scotland against Japan as Rory Darge withdraws injured
teams.body: Head coach Gregor Townsend has changed captain for the second time in a week. Forward Rory Darge, man of the match against Australia while standing in for the ruled-out Sione Tuipulotu, was initially named despite a shoulder injury but will now sit out today's test, the BBC reports. Glasgow centre Stafford McDowall takes the armband six days after being called off his father's farm in Dumfries to face the Wallabies. Matt Fagerson starts at No. 8. Darge stays in the squad, aiming to play next week.

lead.why: A late injury withdrawal and a new captain for today's test is the freshest hard news about the senior side.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy warns Wales one All Blacks win has not fixed everything
teams.body: Wales head coach Steve Tandy is guarding against a hangover before Saturday's Test against Australia, a week after the 35-28 defeat of New Zealand. "We can't assume that because one scoreboard went our way, everything is fixed," he told BBC Sport Wales. He added that his side must double down on recovery, training and executing the core areas of their game. The BBC reports that Wales, ninth in the world rankings, remain slight underdogs against the seventh-ranked Wallabies.

teams.heading: Fabien Pelous recalls Pumas beating hosts France twice at 2007 World Cup
teams.body: France hosted a World Cup for the first time in 2007, and it began and ended with defeat to Argentina — in the opening match at the Stade de France and again in the third-place play-off. Fabien Pelous, 33 and on his last campaign with France, says the hosts were lulled by home enthusiasm and the Pumas got inside their heads, playing hard, ball-hoarding rugby like Bernard Laporte's Stade Français. Agustín Pichot, scrum-half and captain, did everything to unsettle opposite number Jean-Baptiste Elissalde.

lead.why: The Piccardo row and France's selection have already run, and Laporte's reply is a new quote rather than a development, so the Pelous retrospective is the strongest new Argentina item.

teams.heading: Les Kiss keeps eye on Liam Wright as Wales eligibility looms
teams.body: Former Wallabies captain Liam Wright, now an Ospreys flanker, visited the Australia camp in Cardiff this week. Australia head coach Les Kiss, who coached him at the Queensland Reds, did not rule out a recall: "And someone of his calibre, we'll keep an eye on for sure." The 29-year-old has six caps, the last as captain against Wales in July 2024. He becomes Welsh-qualified next summer through a Pembroke Dock grandfather. Wright says he wants a gold jersey but would explore Wales if that door closes.

teams.heading: Japan lose Takeuchi, Tokito and props Tamafusa and Helu before Murrayfield
teams.body: All four are out through injury or condition for Saturday's Nations Championship finale against Scotland, Rugby Asia 247 reports. With both props unavailable, Sojiro Otsuka, Kenji Sato and Ryosuke Iwaihara start up front, while Toyota Verblitz call-up Taufa Latu takes the No. 18 shirt. History offers little comfort: Scotland have won eight of the nine meetings, Japan's lone victory coming at their home 2019 World Cup, and the hosts won 29-20 when the sides last met in Edinburgh.

teams.heading: David Kirk puts Dave Rennie's All Blacks on notice before England Test
teams.body: NZ Rugby chair David Kirk says he would be "pretty disappointed" by defeat at Twickenham, but will judge head coach Dave Rennie's side on performance rather than result: "a bad loss would be concerning." Kirk called this the All Blacks' hardest year, with three of their four defeats coming against the Springboks. He described the fourth, last weekend's 28-35 loss in Cardiff, as a Welsh miracle, and noted New Zealand had just one scrum put-in. Rennie's predecessor, Scott Robertson, was sacked after a loss to England.

lead.why: The NZ Rugby chair putting the All Blacks on notice before England is the freshest hard New Zealand story not already run.

teams.heading: Mzwandile Stick says Prendergast would be learning to tackle if Fijian
teams.body: Springbok assistant coach Mzwandile Stick questioned rugby's disciplinary consistency on Friday after Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast was cleared by an independent panel of an alleged hip-drop tackle that injured Fiji No. 8 Peceli Yato, leaving him free to face South Africa in Dublin. Had the player been Fijian, Stick argued, he would be back in Fiji taking extra tackling lessons. "But it's an Irish player, it's free to play," he said, adding that not one of 17 knee-drop tackles in the France defeat was punished.

lead.why: A Springbok coach's pointed barb about Ireland's cleared fly-half on the eve of the Dublin test is fresh and different from the Erasmus watchalong and selection stories already run.
